title: Adding information to noun phrases (2): prepositional phrases, participle clauses
summary: Как уточнять существительное после него: предложные группы (**the man in the corner**), причастные обороты **-ing / -ed** и инфинитив (**the first person to arrive**).
ru:
## Сокращённая замена придаточного
Придаточное с **who / which / that** можно сократить, убрав местоимение и вспомогательный глагол. Остаётся предложная группа, причастный оборот или инфинитивная группа. Такое словосочетание ставится **сразу после существительного** и делает текст плотнее — особенно в письменном стиле.
> The man **who is standing in the corner** is my lawyer. → The man **in the corner** is my lawyer. — Мужчина в углу — мой адвокат.
> The people **who are waiting outside** are cold. → The people **waiting outside** are cold.
> The report **that was published last week** criticised the government. → The report **published last week** criticised the government.

## Предложные группы
Предлог + существительное после существительного: *the road **to the village**, a book **about whales**, the house **with a red door**, the woman **in the grey suit**, a cup **of tea**, the cost **of living**.* Часто это эквивалент **who is / which has / which is**.
- ~~the man who in the corner~~ → the man **in the corner**

## -ing обороты (действие в процессе)
Действительный залог: **who / which + глагол** → **-ing**. Описывает действие, происходящее сейчас, регулярное или постоянное свойство:
> The students **sitting at the back** couldn't hear. — Студенты, сидевшие на задних рядах, не слышали.
> A law **forbidding** smoking in cars came into force.
> Anyone **wanting** to join should sign up. (= who wants)
Это нельзя использовать для **одного завершённого события** в прошлом: ~~The man breaking the window yesterday was caught.~~ → The man **who broke** the window yesterday was caught.

## -ed обороты (пассив)
Причастие II заменяет **who / which + was / were + причастие**:
> The problems **caused by the storm** will take months to fix. — Проблемы, вызванные бурей, будут устранять месяцами.
> The candidates **invited to the interview** must bring ID.
> a man **named John** · a film **directed by** Ana Lee · the documents **prepared by** the committee
Если действие ещё идёт, используйте **being + -ed**: *the people **being interviewed** now.*

## Инфинитив: first, last, only, best
После **the first / the last / the only / the next / the best** и суперлативов, а также после **place, way, time, something, anything** часто стоит инфинитив:
> She was the first woman **to win** the prize. — Она стала первой женщиной, выигравшей премию.
> Here is a good place **to eat**. — Вот хорошее место, где поесть.
> The best way **to learn** a language is to use it.
- ~~the first woman winning the prize~~ (неидиоматично) → the first woman **to win** the prize

## Прилагательные после существительного
Прилагательные ставятся **после** слов **anyone, anything, something, nothing, somewhere** и т.д.: *Is there anything interesting on TV? I want someone reliable.* Также после существительного, если за прилагательным идёт дополнение: *the only seats available, the people responsible.*
- ~~interesting anything~~ → anything **interesting**

## Запятые
Если информация дополнительная (не определяет объект), её выделяют запятыми: *The report, published last week, criticised the government.* Если же определяет — запятых нет: *The report published last week criticised the government* (а не тот, что вышел раньше).
en:
## A shortened relative clause
A clause with **who / which / that** can be shortened by dropping the pronoun and the auxiliary verb. What remains is a prepositional phrase, a participle clause or an infinitive phrase. It stands **straight after the noun** and makes text denser — especially in writing.
> The man **who is standing in the corner** is my lawyer. → The man **in the corner** is my lawyer.
> The people **who are waiting outside** are cold. → The people **waiting outside** are cold.
> The report **that was published last week** criticised the government. → The report **published last week** criticised the government.

## Prepositional phrases
Preposition + noun after a noun: *the road **to the village**, a book **about whales**, the house **with a red door**, the woman **in the grey suit**, a cup **of tea**, the cost **of living**.* Often equal to **who is / which has / which is**.
- ~~the man who in the corner~~ → the man **in the corner**

## -ing clauses (action in progress)
Active meaning: **who / which + verb** → **-ing**. It describes an action in progress, a repeated action or a permanent feature:
> The students **sitting at the back** couldn't hear.
> A law **forbidding** smoking in cars came into force.
> Anyone **wanting** to join should sign up. (= who wants)
We cannot use it for **one completed event** in the past: ~~The man breaking the window yesterday was caught.~~ → The man **who broke** the window yesterday was caught.

## -ed clauses (passive meaning)
The past participle replaces **who / which + was / were + participle**:
> The problems **caused by the storm** will take months to fix.
> The candidates **invited to the interview** must bring ID.
> a man **named John** · a film **directed by** Ana Lee · the documents **prepared by** the committee
If the action is still going on, use **being + -ed**: *the people **being interviewed** now.*

## Infinitive: first, last, only, best
After **the first / the last / the only / the next / the best** and superlatives, and after **place, way, time, something, anything**, we often use an infinitive:
> She was the first woman **to win** the prize.
> Here is a good place **to eat**.
> The best way **to learn** a language is to use it.
- ~~the first woman winning the prize~~ (unidiomatic) → the first woman **to win** the prize

## Adjectives after the noun
Adjectives go **after** **anyone, anything, something, nothing, somewhere** and so on: *Is there anything interesting on TV? I want someone reliable.* They also follow a noun when they have a complement or limit the noun: *the only seats available, the people responsible.*
- ~~interesting anything~~ → anything **interesting**

## Commas
If the information is extra (doesn't identify), commas surround it: *The report, published last week, criticised the government.* If it identifies, there are no commas: *The report published last week criticised the government* (not an earlier one).
structure:
## Что сокращаем
| Полное придаточное | Краткая форма | Тип |
|---|---|---|
| the man **who is** in the corner | the man **in the corner** | предложная группа |
| the people **who are** waiting | the people **waiting** | **-ing** (действие) |
| the report **that was** published | the report **published** | **-ed** (пассив) |
| the first woman **who won** | the first woman **to win** | инфинитив |
| anything **that is** interesting | anything **interesting** | прилагательное |

## Что выбрать
| Смысл | Форма | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| активное действие | **-ing** | students **sitting** at the back |
| пассив | **-ed** | problems **caused** by the storm |
| пассив, идёт сейчас | **being + -ed** | people **being interviewed** |
| the first / last / only / best, place, way | **to + глагол** | the first person **to arrive** |
| место, обладание, тема | **предлог + сущ.** | a book **about** whales |

## Формулы
> существительное + **-ing** / **-ed** / **to + глагол** / **предлог + существительное**
> **anyone / something / nothing + прилагательное**
> the first / last / only + существительное + **to + глагол**

exercises.title: -ing или -ed?
exercises.instruction: Поставьте глагол в скобках в форму **-ing** или **-ed**.
exercises.example: The people (wait) outside were cold. → The people **waiting** outside were cold.

items.text: The people {{waiting}} outside the building were getting cold. (wait)
The report {{published}} last week criticised the government. (publish)
Anyone {{wanting}} to join the trip should sign up by Friday. (want)
The seats {{reserved}} for VIPs were empty. (reserve)
A law {{forbidding}} smoking in cars came into force in March. (forbid)
The man {{arrested}} yesterday has been released. (arrest)
Most of the students {{taking}} the exam passed. (take)
The problems {{caused}} by the storm will take months to fix. (cause)
She was the first person {{to}} arrive at the meeting.
The woman {{in}} the grey suit is my lawyer.
A house {{with}} a red door stands at the end of the street.
The best way {{to}} learn a language is to use it every day.
The road {{to}} the village is closed because of snow.
Is there a book {{about|on}} Roman history in the library?

items.q: The students ___ at the back couldn't hear.
items.why: Активное действие (= who were sitting) → **-ing** без местоимения и вспомогательного глагола; **were sitting** без **who** превращает фразу во второе сказуемое.

items.q: The email ___ yesterday contained an error.
The documents ___ by the committee are confidential.
items.why: Документы готовит комитет, сами они ничего не делают (пассив) → **-ed**.

items.q: She was the first woman ___ the prize.
Как сократить a man who is named John?
The house ___ a red door is for sale.
items.why: **With** = «имеющий»: the house with a red door.

items.q: Everyone ___ the meeting must register at the desk.
items.why: Активное действие (= who attends / is attending) → **attending**.

items.q: Most of the people ___ in the survey said they were unhappy.
items.why: Людей опросили (пассив, = who were asked) → **asked**; *people asking in the survey* не имеет смысла.

options: The man breaking the window yesterday was caught.
The man who broke the window yesterday was caught.
The man broken the window yesterday was caught.
items.why: Для одного завершённого события в прошлом **-ing** не подходит; нужно придаточное **who broke**.

options: Is there anything interesting on TV?
Is there interesting anything on TV?
Is there anything interestingly on TV?

items.q: The best way ___ the problem is to ask for help.

items.why: **A place + to stay** = «место, где можно остановиться».

items.q: The question ___ in the exam was difficult.
Что значит children living in big cities?
options: children who live in big cities
children to live in big cities

exercises.title: Сократите придаточное
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, заменив придаточное причастием, инфинитивом или предложной группой.

items.prompt: The people who are waiting outside are cold.
answers: The people waiting outside are cold.

items.prompt: The report that was published last week criticised the government.
answers: The report published last week criticised the government.

items.prompt: Anyone who wants to join should sign up.
answers: Anyone wanting to join should sign up.

items.prompt: The problems that were caused by the storm will take months to fix.
answers: The problems caused by the storm will take months to fix.

items.prompt: She was the first woman who won the prize.
answers: She was the first woman to win the prize.

items.prompt: The man who is wearing a grey suit is my lawyer.
answers: The man wearing a grey suit is my lawyer.
The man in a grey suit is my lawyer.
The man in the grey suit is my lawyer.

exercises.title: Объедините предложения
exercises.instruction: Объедините предложения в одно, используя предложную группу, причастие или инфинитив.

items.prompt: A house stands at the end of the road. It has a red door.
answers: A house with a red door stands at the end of the road.

items.prompt: I need a book. It is about Roman history.
answers: I need a book about Roman history.
I need a book on Roman history.

items.prompt: I found a hotel. The hotel is near the station.
answers: I found a hotel near the station.

items.prompt: (Use -ed) The candidates who were invited to the interview must bring ID.
answers: The candidates invited to the interview must bring ID.

items.prompt: (Use to-infinitive) Here is a good place where we can eat.
answers: Here is a good place to eat.
Here's a good place to eat.
Here is a good place for us to eat.
Here's a good place for us to eat.

items.prompt: (Use -ing) A law which forbids smoking in cars came into force.
answers: A law forbidding smoking in cars came into force.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя причастные обороты, инфинитив или предложные группы после существительных.

items.prompt: Describe the people living near you. Use living.
items.sample: The people living next door are very quiet.

items.prompt: Write about a book or an article you have read recently. Use -ed.
items.sample: The article published in last week's paper made me think.

items.prompt: Name the best place to relax in your city.
items.sample: The best place to relax in my city is the botanical garden.

items.prompt: Describe a person in your workplace or class. Use a prepositional phrase (with / in).
items.sample: The woman with the red scarf is our new teacher.

items.prompt: Write about the first or the last person to do something in your family.
items.sample: My sister was the first person in our family to graduate from university.

items.prompt: Write what you want for dinner using something + adjective.
items.sample: I'd like something light and warm for dinner.
